difficulty_why: Slack allows immediate unlisted OAuth distribution across workspaces, but commercial unlisted apps face strict Tier 1 rate limits on conversation history endpoints, and restricted search scopes require Marketplace or partner review.

dev_time.label: 15-30 min
dev_time.text: Creating the Slack app, adding redirect URIs, configuring bot and user scopes, activating public distribution, and retrieving OAuth credentials takes 15 to 30 minutes.

launch_time.label: Same day to 10 weeks
launch_time.text: Unlisted public OAuth distribution is functional immediately on the same day without review; full Marketplace approval to remove commercial rate limits takes up to 10 weeks.

own_app_reasons.label: Custom branding on consent screen
own_app_reasons.text: Display your own product name, logo, and description to users on the Slack OAuth authorization consent screen instead of a third-party intermediary.

own_app_reasons.label: Tailored scope configuration
own_app_reasons.text: Configure the exact bot and user token scopes your application needs rather than relying on standard pre-bundled scopes.

app_type.label: Slack App (OAuth 2.0 / Public Distribution)
app_type.text: Create a standard Slack App 'From scratch' with OAuth v2 configured. By default, new Slack apps are single-workspace; activating Public Distribution (unlisted) enables external workspaces to connect via OAuth without requiring a public Slack Marketplace listing.

prerequisites.label: Slack account & development workspace
prerequisites.text: A Slack account with access to a development workspace where the application can be registered and tested.

prerequisites.label: No paid plan required
prerequisites.text: Developers can create, configure, and test Slack applications on a standard free Slack workspace without a paid subscription.

prerequisites.label: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.text: A valid HTTPS callback URL (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) accessible by the OAuth client.

steps.label: Create Slack App
steps.text: Navigate to https://api.slack.com/apps, sign in to your Slack account, click 'Create New App', select 'From scratch', provide an App Name, and select your development workspace.

fields.label: Pick a workspace to develop your app in

steps.label: Add Redirect URL
steps.text: In the left sidebar under Features, select 'OAuth & Permissions', scroll down to the 'Redirect URLs' section, click 'Add New Redirect URL', enter 'https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add', and click 'Save URLs'.

steps.label: Configure Scopes
steps.text: On the 'OAuth & Permissions' page, scroll down to 'Scopes' and click 'Add an OAuth Scope' under 'Bot Token Scopes' and/or 'User Token Scopes' to add the required permissions.

fields.label: Bot / User Token Scopes
fields.value: calls:read, calls:write, channels:history, channels:read, channels:write, chat:write, dnd:read, dnd:write, emoji:read, files:read, files:write, groups:history, groups:read, groups:write, im:history, im:read, im:write, links:read, links:write, lists:read, lists:write, mpim:history, mpim:read, mpim:write, pins:read, pins:write, reactions:read, reactions:write, reminders:read, reminders:write, remote_files:read, remote_files:share, search:read, search:read.files, search:read.im, search:read.mpim, search:read.private, search:read.public, search:read.users, team:read, usergroups:read, usergroups:write, users.profile:read, users.profile:write, users:read, users:read.email, users:write

steps.label: Enable Public Distribution
steps.text: In the left navigation sidebar under Settings, click 'Manage Distribution', complete any required checklist items (such as adding an app description), and click 'Activate Public Distribution' to allow any external workspace to authorize the app.

steps.label: Obtain OAuth Credentials
steps.text: In the left navigation sidebar under Settings, click 'Basic Information', scroll to 'App Credentials', and copy the 'Client ID' and 'Client Secret' to input into your Composio integration settings.

scopes.label: Restricted search scopes
scopes.text: search:read, search:read.files, search:read.im, search:read.mpim, search:read.private, search:read.public, search:read.users: restricted and prohibited for standard Marketplace apps without special partnership.

scopes.label: History scopes subject to rate throttling
scopes.text: channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history: require justification in review; unlisted commercial apps face Tier 1 (1 req/min) rate limits until reviewed.

scopes.label: Standard messaging and files scopes
scopes.text: chat:write, files:read, files:write, remote_files:read, remote_files:share: standard bot and user scopes usable immediately via OAuth distribution without pre-review.

scopes.label: Channel management scopes
scopes.text: channels:read, channels:write, groups:read, groups:write, im:read, im:write, mpim:read, mpim:write: standard channel scopes available upon user/admin installation consent.

scopes.label: User directory and identity scopes
scopes.text: users:read, users:read.email, users:write, users.profile:read, users.profile:write, team:read, usergroups:read, usergroups:write: standard scopes for accessing profile and workspace details.

scopes.label: Utility and interaction scopes
scopes.text: calls:read, calls:write, dnd:read, dnd:write, emoji:read, links:read, links:write, lists:read, lists:write, pins:read, pins:write, reactions:read, reactions:write, reminders:read, reminders:write: standard feature scopes.

approval.label: When required
approval.text: Slack Marketplace review is required only to be listed in the public directory; apps can distribute to external workspaces immediately without review by activating Public Distribution under Manage Distribution.

approval.label: What's checked
approval.text: Slack evaluates least privilege scope usage, end-to-end installation and onboarding user experience, test account credentials, HTTPS/SSL endpoints, privacy policy, and landing page quality.

approval.label: Wait
approval.text: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days for initial feedback, and full functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions (up to 6 weeks for app updates).

approval.label: Cost
approval.text: Slack does not charge any fee for Slack Marketplace submission, review, or app directory inclusion.

approval.label: Common rejections
approval.text: Rejections occur for requesting restricted scopes such as search:read or admin.*, using Slack data to train LLMs, message backup/export use cases, functional bugs, or failing the active workspace minimum.

approval.label: Before approval
approval.text: Before submitting for Marketplace review, the app must already be installed and active on at least 5 to 10 active workspaces used within the past 28 days.

approval.label: Install cap before review
approval.text: Slack does not enforce a numerical cap on the number of workspaces that can install an unlisted app via public OAuth distribution.

approval.label: Limits until reviewed
approval.text: Unlisted commercial apps face conversations.history and conversations.replies rate limits reduced to Tier 1 (1 request per minute, max 15 messages per call), and Marketplace listing is designated as the sanctioned channel for commercial distribution.

pitfalls.label: Exact redirect URI match
pitfalls.text: The redirect_uri parameter must match one of the configured HTTPS Redirect URLs and must be identical in both the authorize request and token exchange call; otherwise a bad_redirect_uri error occurs.

pitfalls.label: Bot vs user scopes separation
pitfalls.text: Slack separates bot scopes (scope parameter) and user scopes (user_scope parameter); mixing Sign in with Slack user scopes with non-SIWS scopes in the same flow triggers a scope conflict.

pitfalls.label: Restricted search scopes
pitfalls.text: Requesting search:read or search:read.* makes an app ineligible for general Marketplace approval unless granted access via specialized partner APIs.

pitfalls.label: LLM training prohibition
pitfalls.text: Using customer data retrieved from Slack APIs to train Large Language Models is strictly prohibited under Slack Marketplace developer policies.

pitfalls.label: Scope updates require reinstallation
pitfalls.text: Adding scopes in app settings updates only future authorization requests; previously connected workspaces retain old scopes until users re-authorize.

pitfalls.label: Active workspace prerequisite gate
pitfalls.text: Apps must have at least 5 to 10 active workspaces used within the past 28 days before Slack's portal allows submitting for Marketplace review.

support.label: Slack developer support email
support.text: Contact Slack developer support directly by sending an email to support@slack.com.

support.label: Slack API documentation
support.text: Consult official developer documentation, tutorials, and endpoint references at api.slack.com and docs.slack.dev.

support.label: Slack partner support
support.text: For high-volume partner or commercial integration assistance, contact partnersupport@slack-corp.com.

email_subject: Slack OAuth 2.0 Integration & Commercial Distribution Inquiry - [Your App Name]
email_body:
Hi Slack Developer Relations Team,

We are developing an AI agent application that integrates with Slack via OAuth 2.0 to help our users interact with channels, send messages, and manage files on their workspaces.

Our application uses standard bot and user OAuth scopes, along with conversation reading permissions. We would appreciate clarification on the following:
1. Are there specific review or partnership requirements for our app if we request history or search scopes for our users?
2. For commercial multi-workspace distribution, what is the current timeline and process for Marketplace review to ensure our app is not restricted by Tier 1 history rate limits?
3. What verification or test credentials should we prepare to facilitate a smooth onboarding and review process?
